alternatives_and_negative_results: Do not divide or round the threshold, use floating arithmetic in RTL, wrap products, or change equality to >=.
applicability: RTL CA-CFAR and its future SCR/clutter qualification.
assessed_root_cause: The decision is a rational integer inequality; exact product widths and strictness are part of the acceptance contract.
author_role: historical project engineering record, backfilled by FPGA engineering copilot
chosen_corrective_method: Use full unsigned cross-products at approved widths, guard the full intermediate products, preserve the 7x7-minus-3x3 training geometry and no-wrap edges.
generalizable_lesson: When the threshold is rational, implement its exact integer inequality and prove operand widths rather than approximating with floating arithmetic.
initial_faulty_assumption_or_design_deci: Floating threshold division or implicit rounding could alter equality behavior and alarm decisions at the threshold.
non_applicability: Does not prove the clutter source population or statistical Pfa outside approved scope.
observable_consequence: C05 native engine uses U46.30 power, U52.30 SUM40 and strict 40*Pcut*65536 > 490007*SUM40; equality is NO ALARM; 2,782 valid CUTs are checked.
observed_problem: The CFAR decision depends on exact integer CUT power, 40 training cells, a rational alpha and edge-validity geometry.
repeatable_validation: Test exact equality and plus/minus one integer boundaries, all valid CUT coordinates, 40 training cells, and independent Fraction comparisons.
reviewer_role: documentary evidence validation by FPGA engineering copilot; not a separate human reviewer
safety_contract_constraints: Alpha 490007/65536, 40 training cells, 2,782 CUT geometry and strict greater-than comparator remain frozen.
title: Implement CA-CFAR as exact unsigned cross-products with frozen geometry
